prerequisites: Having fully passed the 1st year of the degree

learning_outcomes.text: Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate, and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them by working in multidisciplinary teams.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess learning skills that allow for continuous lifelong learning for adequate professional development.
Ability to express oneself correctly orally and in writing in different situations and forums, using the conventions of different textual genres.
Effective communication, both written and oral, of knowledge, procedures, results, and ideas.
Ability to work in unidisciplinary, multidisciplinary, or multicultural teams.
Ability to adapt and understand other cultures and situations.
Ability to analyze, criticize, and synthesize.

syllabus_topics: Ways to organize discourse. Argumentation techniques.
Some types of written genres: memoirs, reports, academic papers.
teaching_methods: STEAM projects with written and oral tasks
Walk&Talk methodology (experiential learning combining walking and collaborative dialogue)

assessment_methods.method: Final Exam (Written and Oral Part) (Global Assessment)

assessment_rules: For continuous/progressive evaluation, the final grade consists of a written part (70%) and an oral part (30%), with both parts needing to be passed separately. The global final evaluation and the extraordinary (resit) evaluation are also structured into a written part (70%) and an oral part (30%), requiring both to be passed. The grade for these evaluations is obtained through a written exam and an oral presentation. All evaluation tests are graded out of 10.
